title: Tagged releases: binaries, multi-architecture image, changelog
description: Pushing a version tag builds and publishes a release: Linux amd64 and arm64 binaries with checksums on GitHub Releases, and a multi-architecture image on GitHub Container Registry tagged with the version and `latest`. Use GoReleaser (or an equivalent the implementer justifies). Generate release notes from merged changes and keep a CHANGELOG.md with an 'Upgrade notes' section per version. Attach build provenance so a club can verify an image came from this repository. The release compose file references the published image by version instead of building locally.
acceptance_criteria: Pushing tag vX.Y.Z produces a GitHub Release with two binaries, a checksum file and notes, and a ghcr.io image for both architectures
The running app reports exactly that version
CHANGELOG.md exists with an entry for the first release and an upgrade-notes convention
Images carry provenance attestations and standard OCI labels (source, version, licence)
The release job only runs after CI passes on the tagged commit
A pre-release tag (v0.x or -rc) publishes without moving `latest`
RELEASING.md describes cutting a release in under ten steps

notes: The package on ghcr.io must be set public once, by hand, in GitHub settings.
Check the current GoReleaser and docker/build-push-action documentation for configuration syntax.

testing_requirements: Cut v0.9.0-rc1 and install it from the published image on a clean machine

context.user_story: As a club operator, I want to install and upgrade by version number.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
